paper_title: AttentionInfluence Adopting Attention Head Influence for Weak-to-Strong   Pretraining Data Selection
caption: The statistics of clustering. The left is the clustering result of AttentionInfluence, the right part is that of FineWeb-Edu Classifier.
model_annotation: This figure presents two side-by-side sunburst/nested pie charts comparing clustering results between two methods: AttentionInfluence (left) and FineWeb-Edu Classifier (right). Each chart uses a two-level ring structure, where the inner ring represents broader category groupings and the outer ring represents finer sub-categories with associated numeric values (likely percentages or proportions). The AttentionInfluence chart (left) shows an inner ring with categories including Education (25, green), History & Society (23, orange), Health & Medicine (22, blue), Science (15, pink/red), Tech & Engineer (12, light blue), and Fin & Law (3, yellow). The outer ring breaks these into subcategories: Teaching & resources (15), Science & technology education (10), Diseases (11), Nutrition (5), Medical (6), Animal & Plant (13), Materials (2), Historical review (7), Society & culture (10), Events & people (6), Infor tech (5), Emerging tech (4), Materials (3), Manage (2), Policy (1). The FineWeb-Edu Classifier chart (right) shows an inner ring with Education (38, green), History & Society (19, orange), Health & Medicine (19, blue), Science (15, pink/red), and Tech & Engineer (8, light blue). The outer ring includes: Teaching & resources (17), Healthy education (2), Science & technology education (19), Diseases (10), Nutrition (7), Medical (2), Animal & Plant (12), Materials (3), Historical review (12), Society & culture (5), Events & people (2), Infor tech (3), Materials (1), Emerging tech (4), Manage (1). Notably, in the right chart, Education (38) occupies a substantially larger proportion compared to the left chart (25), while History & Society decreases from 23 to 19. Labels with numeric values are placed on or around each slice with leader lines pointing to smaller segments. No separate legend is provided; instead, labels are directly annotated on the chart. The color scheme is consistent between both charts, with green representing Education, orange for History & Society, blue for Health & Medicine, pink/red for Science, and light blue for Tech & Engineer.
